title: Active learning guides experimental design of lead-free solder alloys
summary: Uncertainty-aware Gaussian-process models and multi-objective Bayesian acquisition guided seven design–experiment iterations. The study reports two selected alloys, Si-4 and Se-5, tested for tensile strength and fracture elongation. Reported averages follow the authors’ stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests. Performance was mixed: the tested samples had poorer wettability and solder-joint shear strength than the commercial comparator. This is one laboratory alloy-design campaign, not evidence of industrial deployment or across-the-board superiority.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process models; multi-objective Bayesian active learning
organization: Shanghai University; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

source_review.scope: Primary npj Computational Materials indexed full text, publication history, experimental characterization and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: Seven design–experiment iterations included tensile testing of selected Si-4 and Se-5 alloys and evaluation of additional solder properties against a commercial comparator.
evidence.unknown: Averages follow a stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests; wettability and joint shear strength were worse than the comparator. No industrial deployment or independent replication was established.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process models represented experimental uncertainty and Bayesian multi-objective acquisition selected compositions for successive synthesis and testing rounds.
